beats.trigger: Building Agent Systems
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: A system remembers, grows, and compounds. Chat doesn't.
beats.got: A slogan. No cost, no number.

beats.trigger: (1) Bring a live challenge.
beats.got: Five prework items, two of which need IT to have connected systems I have no say over.

beats.trigger: Evaluate whether memory is compounding or growing
beats.got: There's an 'evaluate' item, but I can't tell yet what it's measured against.

beats.trigger: What's the difference between asking an LLM a question and having an LLM maintain a knowledge base for you?
beats.got: Asking once versus having it keep notes. I don't yet see why I'd pay for the second.

beats.trigger: If everything you've read and drafted on that challenge moved into a memory an agent could read and sharpen, what changes at work?
beats.got: A hypothetical with no figure attached. Pick a real challenge, though: the board capex paper.

beats.trigger: The guardrail: propose or draft only, do not send, edit, book, or change anything.
beats.got: The risk is named up front and the agent can only draft. That I can sign off on.

beats.trigger: The Q2 pricing redesign: usage-based vs. seats, pilot cohort, sales briefing.
beats.got: A good challenge is a real deliverable with an owner. Mine is the board capex paper.

beats.trigger: Keep it narrow enough that 5–8 topic pages cover it.
beats.got: A bounded scope: 5-8 pages, not the whole company.

beats.trigger: Always comply with your company's AI policy.
beats.got: The data and policy question gets raised before I have to ask it. Finance data stays out for now.

beats.trigger: Ask for a plan first.
beats.got: Make it show a plan before it reads a lot of files. Reads cost money.

beats.trigger: Push back, sharpen, add what's missing.
beats.got: I correct the source list before anything is pulled in.

beats.trigger: You don't copy-paste.
beats.got: The agent pulls the files in itself, so it saves some clerical work.

beats.trigger: Read the plan before saying go.
beats.got: I approve before it writes. Basic control, good.

beats.trigger: That list is your first quality check.
beats.got: It lists its own gaps. Useful, though a self-audit is not an independent audit.

beats.trigger: Citations show whether the agent read the memory or the LLM filled in from training data.
beats.got: I can check where an answer came from. That is the first thing here I can verify.

beats.trigger: A good knowledge base sharpens: pages get tighter as new sources arrive, not longer.
beats.got: It updates pages instead of piling on. I'd want to see a before and after.

beats.trigger: Reject the ones that miss; the agent applies the ones you approve.
beats.got: It proposes and I approve, so changes only happen with my say-so.

beats.trigger: If the answer is specific and every claim has a citation, the memory works.
beats.got: A pass/fail test I can run myself. Specific plus cited means it works.

beats.trigger: Chat doesn't do this.
beats.got: Files persist and a chat thread doesn't. Fair, but still no cost per month.

beats.trigger: The second batch made the first batch better.
beats.got: More input improved the earlier pages. Plausible, and it needs a measure.

beats.trigger: A saved document with no agent is just a document.
beats.got: Files plus an agent that reads them. That is all a system is, apparently.

beats.trigger: the ones that couldn't survive got cut
beats.got: Weak claims get dropped when old and new meet. It's a mechanism, but I'd audit what got cut.

beats.trigger: Keep the rules small and boring.
beats.got: Nothing new. Boring rules are how I run month-end.

beats.trigger: No database, special tool or paid tier is needed.
beats.got: Little to buy, and no lock-in since it's plain text. That changes the cost question, though it still has no figure.

beats.trigger: Sharpen the memory, never the sources, or you lose the evidence.
beats.got: Originals stay untouched and only the working layer changes. That is an audit trail.

beats.trigger: so they belong to the memory you built, not the LLM behind it.
beats.got: The value sits in my files, not in the vendor's model. That cuts against my idea of buying a licence.

beats.trigger: If a competitor could claim a page, the memory is growing but not compounding.
beats.got: Generic pages are a warning sign. Fine, but it's a vibe test.

beats.trigger: Most of what you know about your company sits in heads and corridors, and nobody has written it down.
beats.got: The agent only knows what's written down. My controller's head is not in any file.

beats.trigger: The agent writes the rules file from the session: what worked, what rubbed, what got repeated.
beats.got: A retro that turns into a rules file. Process again.

beats.trigger: What the agent leaves out is often the signal.
beats.got: Check what the summary omits. Same as reading a management report.

beats.trigger: Every miss turns into a line of context that stops the next miss.
beats.got: Each error becomes a standing rule. That is how controls work.

beats.trigger: The model will change under this. The memory will not.
beats.got: Models are swappable and the lasting asset is our own folder. I'd been thinking of the tool as the asset.

beats.trigger: Plain text: models read and write text best.
beats.got: Three bullets I could repeat to the CEO.

beats.trigger: Module 3 splits work against that week of runs; without it the split is guesswork.
beats.got: There's homework. A week of daily runs I probably won't do.

beats.trigger: Pick the one you would read tomorrow morning.
beats.got: Three jobs on offer. The daily risk scan is the only one I'd read.

beats.trigger: Without a calendar connector, use a calendar screenshot or exported agenda.
beats.got: Connecting my work account is an IT decision, so I'd use the screenshot route.

beats.trigger: Give your daily output the look and feel of your company's website (colours, typography, headers, voice).
beats.got: Nothing I care about. Fonts and colours for a morning page, with no cost or benefit.

beats.trigger: Have the agent interview you on the job, output shape and hard boundary, then write its instruction file.
beats.got: I state the job and the hard limit once and it writes the instructions down.

beats.trigger: Double-click `module-2/morning-agent/latest.html` to open it in your browser.
beats.got: Setup is a fair number of clicks, and I don't see the per-run cost.

beats.trigger: For the first three days, don't retune.
beats.got: Watch it for a week before judging. Reasonable, but it asks for my time.

beats.trigger: A memory that sits there is a document.
beats.got: It only pays off if it runs on a schedule and I react to the output.

beats.trigger: for noticing when work should call the agent.
beats.got: More reading before the next module.

beats.trigger: Not toy demos.
beats.got: Forty minutes of blog posts by individual practitioners, none of them a finance function or a Nordic company. I'm not doing that.

beats.trigger: Keep the first version proposal-only: the agent drafts, ranks, or prepares; you decide what leaves the system.
beats.got: Start with agents that only draft, and I keep the decision.

take_homes: Keep the working memory as plain files we own, so the model can be swapped and our material stays. This is the main thing I'm taking home.
An agent that only drafts, with a person deciding what leaves the system, is something I can approve. The agent's work is only trustworthy if the answer is specific and every claim is cited.
The module never gave me a cost per month or a payback figure, so I can't defend any of this to the board yet.

monday.move: Ask my controller to run the month-end variance commentary through an agent once, draft only, using last month's closed numbers.
monday.when: After month-end close, once IT has said yes
monday.stop_condition: Stop if the draft cites nothing checkable, or if correcting it takes longer than writing the commentary ourselves.
monday.blocker: IT has not approved the tool for finance data.

misconception.why: 'The model will change under this. The memory will not.' Together with 'No database, special tool or paid tier is needed' it makes the folder, not the licence, the thing we keep. I still can't price it, so I'm only half convinced.

one_line: The citations and the draft-only guardrail were useful, but it never gave me a cost or a payback figure, and forty minutes of blog reading is not a plan.
